content: # Convergence of single-valued fixed-point iteration for Gibbs-form equilibrium operators This file contains the open problem on Convergence of single-valued fixed-point iteration for Gibbs-form equilibrium operators. --- ## 1. Convergence of single-valued fixed-point iteration for Gibbs-form equilibrium operators Source paper authors: Erhan Bayraktar, Yu‐Jui Huang, Zhenhua Wang, Zhou Zhou ### 1. Problem Background Consider a discrete-time infinite-horizon Markov decision process (MDP) with finite state space $S=\{1,\dots,d\}$ and compact action space $U\subset \mathbb{R}^\ell$ with $0<\mathrm{Leb}(U)<\infty$. A relaxed (randomized) feedback control is a map $\pi:S\to \mathcal{P}(U)$, where $\mathcal{P}(U)$ denotes probability measures on $U$. For $\lambda>0$, an entropy-regularized objective is used in which the stage payoff includes a Shannon differential entropy term. Under entropy regularization, the equilibrium (in the sense of intra-personal subgame-perfect equilibrium for time-inconsistent discounting) can be characterized as a fixed point of a single-valued operator of Gibbs (softmax) form. More concretely, for each state $i\in S$ and vector $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, define a probability density $\Gamma_\lambda(y,i)\in \mathcal{D}(U)$ by $$ \Gamma_\lambda(y,i)(u):=\frac{\exp\left(\frac{1}{\lambda}(f(0,i,u)+p_i^u\cdot y)\right)}{\int_U \exp\left(\frac{1}{\lambda}(f(0,i,v)+p_i^v\cdot y)\right)\,dv},\qquad u\in U, $$ where $f(0,i,u)$ is the one-step reward (at time-difference $0$) and $p_i^u\in\mathbb{R}^d$ is the transition-probability row vector from state $i$ under action $u$. Given $y$, the corresponding relaxed control is $\Gamma_\lambda(y,\cdot):S\to \mathcal{P}(U)$. Let $J_\lambda^\pi$ be the entropy-regularized value functional and let $V_\lambda^\pi\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be the associated continuation-value vector (expected future discounted reward plus discounted entropy starting one step ahead). Define the induced single-valued self-map $\Psi_\lambda:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ by $$ \Psi_\lambda(y):=V_\lambda^{\Gamma_\lambda(y,\cdot)}. $$ Fixed points $y^\star$ of $\Psi_\lambda$ correspond to entropy-regularized relaxed equilibria $\pi^\star=\Gamma_\lambda(y^\star,\cdot)$. A natural numerical approach is fixed-point iteration on $\Psi_\lambda$ (equivalently on the policy operator $\Phi_\lambda(\pi):=\Gamma_\lambda(V_\lambda^\pi,\cdot)$), i.e., start from some $y_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$ (or $\pi_0$) and generate $y_{n+1}=\Psi_\lambda(y_n)$ (or $\pi_{n+1}=\Phi_\lambda(\pi_n)$). ### 2. Open Problem **Question 1.1.** Give conditions under which the single-valued fixed-point iteration $$ y_{n+1}=\Psi_\lambda(y_n)\qquad (n\ge 0) $$ converges (e.g., from arbitrary initialization, or from some specified set of initial points) to a fixed point $y^\star\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $\Psi_\lambda(y^\star)=y^\star$, equivalently producing a regular relaxed equilibrium $\pi^\star=\Gamma_\lambda(y^\star,\cdot)$ for the entropy-regularized time-inconsistent MDP. ### 3. Known Results In Bayraktar–Huang–Wang–Zhou (2024), entropy regularization turns the equilibrium best-response into a single-valued Gibbs map $\Gamma_\lambda$, yielding a single-valued equilibrium operator $\Psi_\lambda(y)=V^{\Gamma_\lambda(y,\cdot)}_\lambda$. Existence of fixed points is obtained via Brouwer after establishing uniform logarithmic entropy bounds (Lemma 2.1) under Lipschitz dependence on actions and a uniform cone condition on $U$. The paper explicitly leaves open the convergence of the naive fixed-point iteration $y_{n+1}=\Psi_\lambda(y_n)$ (Remark 2.6), which would make the approximation-by-regularization approach fully rigorous as a computational method. Among forward citations, the closest progress on iteration convergence is in “Equilibrium for Time-inconsistent Mean Field Games: A Systematic Analysis by Entropy Regularization”, which proves contraction and convergence of a Gibbs-form policy-iteration map $\Phi_\lambda$ under restrictive conditions (small horizon and weak terminal interaction) in a continuous-time finite-horizon mean-field setting. This suggests that proving convergence in the discrete-time infinite-horizon finite-state MDP likely requires additional structure ensuring that $\Psi_\lambda$ (or $\Phi_\lambda$) is a contraction or at least has a globally attracting fixed point—e.g., strong discounting/mixing, small effective horizon $\sum_t \delta(t)$, or quantitative Lipschitz bounds on $y\mapsto V^{\Gamma_\lambda(y,\cdot)}_\lambda$ combined with the $1/\lambda$-Lipschitz nature of the softmax map. Other citing works mainly develop existence/approximation theories via entropy regularization and Schauder/Kakutani fixed points (including mean-field stopping and diffusion-control analogues) but do not establish general convergence of the fixed-point iteration for the Gibbs operator. Therefore, based on the provided forward-citation set, the convergence problem for single-valued fixed-point iteration of $\Psi_\lambda$ in the Bayraktar–Huang–Wang–Zhou discrete-time infinite-horizon setting remains open. #### 3.1 Upstream solution and partial-progress records - [Partial progress #136 (PDF)](https://pranav-nuti.github.io/open-problems-in-or/data/llm_math_export/solution_progress/W4403683873_p0/partial_progress/136.pdf) ### 4.
